answer: Randomized liveness spot-checks make puppet fleets costly to keep alive. Each epoch the protocol pings a random sample of identities with a fresh nonce and a short reply window; a missed check suspends earning until the account re-verifies and pays a fee. An operator tending a garden of puppets must keep every one online and latency-ready around the clock, since checks land anywhere on the voyage of epochs. Centralized signing shows up as correlated response times and flags the fleet. Honest agents answer rare pings from an oasis of routine, paying nothing beyond attention.
